clue.text: Most disreputable group includes man of fashion

indicators.note: the group takes the fashion man inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a set is a group of people or things
Sir Hardy Amies was a British fashion designer, dressmaker to the Queen

explanation.surface: The shadiest gang of all has a fashion designer among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'includes' as the container signal, the fashion man is Hardy Amies, a London couturier best known for dressing Queen Elizabeth II; solvers outside Britain may not know the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamy means sordid or unpleasant, so the superlative describes whatever is the most squalid and shady.

clue.text: Two things occupying lawyers, one taken on holiday

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, something a lawyer works on
a case is a legal matter that keeps a lawyer busy

explanation.surface: Lawyers are kept busy by two matters, one of which goes away with them on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: lawyers handle suits and cases, and the two words joined make the luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed bag of clothes is the item travellers carry with them when they go away.

clue.text: A Welsh girl of Indian descent, say?

parts.note: Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from Wales is described as having roots in India.
explanation.walkthrough: SIAN is the Welsh form of Jane. The question mark and 'say' show that Indian descent is only one example of the wider term.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of Indian descent is one example of a person from the continent stretching from India to Japan.

clue.text: Electrical device in home — are timers properly adjusted?

indicators.note: the letters are set right, put into their correct new order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether the timers on a household appliance have been set correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly adjusted' rearranges the fifteen letters of IN HOME ARE TIMERS. The clue's mention of timers fits the scene, since a hot-water tank is often run on one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the electric element fitted in a hot-water tank to warm the water in a house.

clue.text: Money to cover charge for bread

indicators.note: the money goes around the charge, covering it on both sides

parts.note: a sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Someone needs cash to pay a fee for some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' signals the container. 'Money' is a fair stand-in for a single coin: the Japanese sen, one hundredth of a yen, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a rich German fruit loaf, traditionally eaten at Christmas.

clue.text: Some broccoli by tradition wrapped in paper

indicators.note: the tradition is enclosed by the paper, as food is wrapped in newspaper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
lore is a body of traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Some broccoli is wrapped in newspaper, as tradition dictates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped in' signals the container. The paper is the Financial Times, a pink-paged London daily, and the surface's chip-shop habit of wrapping food in newspaper disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small head of a flowering vegetable is a floret, the part served from a head of broccoli or cauliflower.

clue.text: Ray got going once this initial order was given

definitions.text: Ray got going once this initial order was given

parts.words: Ray got going once this initial order was given
parts.note: the first command in Genesis, which brought light into being: the very first ray started up once it was spoken

explanation.surface: A beam of light began only after the very first command was issued.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'initial order' is the first command of Creation in the Book of Genesis, and the 'ray' is the light that followed it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first thing God commands is that light should exist, a phrase now quoted for any beginning.

clue.text: Biblical advice to sluggard looking back

definitions.meaning: Proverbs tells the lazy man to go to the ant and consider her ways, so the advice is to consider the ant
a heraldic term for a beast whose head faces behind it

explanation.surface: Scripture tells an idler to look at the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Proverbs 6:6 reads 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways'. Split as two words, the answer means 'consider (the) ant'; as one, it is the heraldic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic animal shown with its head turned to face backwards over its shoulder is described with this term; the first reading is a split into regard plus ant.

clue.text: Period of frenzy over crucial land

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: the rut is the mating season of deer, a time of frenzied activity
key means crucial or vital

explanation.surface: A spell of wild excitement surrounds some vital territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the frenzied period round, as a down clue reads upwards. 'land' could suggest a verb, to come ashore, but here it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a country straddling Europe and Asia, so it is a land.

clue.text: Clever revolutionary soldiers hiding in passage

indicators.note: the soldiers are tucked away inside the passage, so one goes in the other

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine

indicators.note: something that revolves is turned round, so the soldiers are read backwards

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Smart rebel troops are lying low in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the soldiers round and 'hiding in' signals the container. 'Revolutionary' looks like it describes the soldiers' politics, and an adit is a mining word solvers meet mainly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick, a synonym of clever in the sense of deft.

clue.text: Man with identity initially revealed by way of speaking

indicators.note: the identity piece is put at the start, ahead of the Man piece

parts.note: ID is short for identity, as on an ID card
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man's identity is finally exposed through the way he talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM; 'initially' puts ID before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic expression or turn of phrase in a language.

clue.text: Aged sort possibly overwhelming learner?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swamp the learner, going around it
a possible version of the words means they may be rearranged into another order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An elderly type might well swamp a beginner with experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AGED SORT and 'overwhelming' puts L inside, after the O. The whole clue also describes the answer: a veteran's experience outweighs a novice's.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is someone long experienced in some activity, a veteran rather than a novice.

clue.text: Singer of carol not somehow keeping time

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the time inside them, holding it
done somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer of a Christmas song somehow fails to keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CAROL NOT, and 'keeping' holds T inside. The surface suggests a singer who cannot keep time, but the time is kept, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, or a woman who sings in that range.

clue.text: Bath or sedgefield? See one there

definitions.text: Bath or sedgefield? See one there

indicators.note: one of these can be seen within the words Bath or sedgefield, spanning them

explanation.surface: Asked about two English towns, you are told what you will see at either.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'batH OR SEdgefield'. Bath and Sedgefield are both English racecourses, so the whole clue also defines the animal seen there.
explanation.definitionFit: Racecourses are where thoroughbreds run, so one is the animal you see at Bath or Sedgefield.

clue.text: Stop in camp?

definitions.meaning: a stopping place on a railway or bus line
a military post or base, or an Australian sheep farm, is a place where people are encamped

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to halt at an encampment.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has both senses: a place where trains stop, and a post where troops or workers are based.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway halt and a military post where people are based both go by this name.

clue.text: What star gets from fans, offering a party piece?

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a ration is a portion, a piece of a larger supply

explanation.surface: A celebrity performs a party piece and wins the fans' love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party piece' looks like one phrase, a turn performed at parties to entertain, but it splits into two separate pieces; 'offering' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans give a star devoted worship and admiration, the intense love the word describes.

clue.text: Deposit of salt recurring

indicators.note: the salt comes round again, giving it twice in a row

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and so is an old salt

explanation.surface: Salt keeps on being deposited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is a sailor, not the mineral the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartar is a hard deposit that forms on teeth, or the crust left in wine casks.

clue.text: Source of water precious, as they say, for wild animal

indicators.note: as people say it means the words are spoken, sounding like another word

parts.note: rain is a source of water; dear means precious or beloved

explanation.surface: A creature of the wild is treasured as a supply of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as they say' turns RAIN DEAR into the animal by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are large deer of the Arctic, found wild in herds as well as domesticated.

clue.text: Good French material used for making hat

parts.note: bon is French for good
net is an open-mesh fabric

explanation.surface: Fine French fabric goes into making a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' tells you to put 'Good' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat tied under the chin, worn by women and babies.

clue.text: Hit the hay with rat on

definitions.meaning: to go to bed, an idiom from sleeping on hay
to inform on someone, for example by handing them over to the police

explanation.surface: Someone goes to bed accompanied by a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like the animal, but 'rat on' is a phrasal verb meaning betray.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both going to bed for the night and handing a wrongdoer over to the authorities.

clue.text: Character with not much to hide as a frequent visitor

indicators.note: the character conceals the small amount, holding it inside

parts.note: hue can mean aspect or character, as in a political hue
a bit is a small amount, not much

explanation.surface: Someone with little to conceal is a regular caller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' puts A BIT inside HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular at a place, someone who goes there often, from the French for accustomed.

clue.text: Courtesan wanting goddess to accept one of her letters

indicators.note: the goddess takes the letter in, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the goddess's own

explanation.surface: A kept woman lacks a goddess to receive one of her letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' signals the container. 'her letters' are Greek ones, since Hera is a Greek goddess; 'wanting' is a link meaning 'needing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hetaera was a highly educated courtesan of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Many unnatural shocks for this VIP?

parts.note: big means large in number or amount
a wig is a false head of hair; a shock is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: An important person suffers a great many unnatural shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocks' are masses of hair, not jolts. Judges and other dignitaries traditionally wore large wigs, hence the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Important people were once marked out by large wigs, so the slang term means a person of importance.

clue.text: Aggrieved one coming to judge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A wronged person comes forward to judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' places RATE after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, the feeling of someone who has been wronged and resents it.

clue.text: Toy boy talked incessantly

parts.note: a rattle is a baby's toy
Don is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young man kept by an older woman chattered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy boy' reads as one phrase, a much younger lover, but it splits into a toy and a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on rattling means to chatter on and on without stopping.

clue.text: Label put on excellent port

parts.note: to dub is to give a name or label to
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A label is stuck on some fine port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine, but it is a harbour city in the United Arab Emirates; 'put on' is a charade link, and A1 has its 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a city on the Persian Gulf with one of the world's busiest harbours.

clue.text: Instil awe when this part of one's body is fantastic!

indicators.note: being fantastic means fanciful or wildly altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trim middle is a thing to marvel at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fantastic' rearranges INSTIL AWE; the exclamation reads as a compliment to a trim figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The waistline is the narrow middle of the body, where a belt goes.

clue.text: Actor's half-hearted speech coming over incoherently

definitions.note: the clue reads Actor is, so the possessive stands for is

indicators.note: half of the heart, the doubled middle letters, is taken away

parts.note: gabble is rapid, unintelligible talk

explanation.surface: A performer's lukewarm lines come across as garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star. 'half-hearted' drops one of the two Bs at the centre of GABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was the American film star of Gone with the Wind, so he is an actor.

clue.text: Groups senior officer left abandoned

indicators.note: the officer has the left letter abandoned, dropped from him

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A top officer leaves some units behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, but it gives L, which 'abandoned' removes from GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification grouping species, and this is its plural.

clue.text: Less significant wannabe trailing after mate

indicators.note: the wannabe follows behind the mate, coming second

parts.note: pal means mate or friend
a trier is someone who tries hard, like a wannabe

explanation.surface: An aspiring hanger-on matters less than the friend he follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailing after' fixes the order of the charade. A 'wannabe' is someone eager to succeed, so a trier is a fair if loose match.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or meagre, so the comparative describes something of smaller importance.
